90yearslong: The new lieutenant gave his name as Arno Yearslong. The corporal looked at his boots, then at the mud, and laughed for the first time in a week.
The Hegemony flag went up over Blackwater Canal. Arno Yearslong did not cheer. He sat down on a sandbag and ate his ration slowly, like a man with time again.
alex_h5315: After 9 days of war, Q-F1 had a place for everything. On Day 9, the men rearranged a shelf to make a place for Hugo "Brick" Alex.
The Hegemony won Blackwater Canal. In Q-F1, Hugo "Brick" Alex listened to three explanations and trusted none of them.
aruuki_045: After 9 days of war, Q-F11 had a place for everything. On Day 9, the men rearranged a shelf to make a place for Albin "Saint" Aruuki.

Albin "Saint" Aruuki had just lit a cigarette at Q-F11 when a bullet cut a line across his cheek. He finished the cigarette before going to the medic. Shot by Rafael "Brick" Firekeyboard of the Concord (@firekeyboard). News that the Hegemony had taken Blackwater Canal reached Albin "Saint" Aruuki during supper. The same stew suddenly tasted better.
bark_passenger: The new lieutenant gave his name as Arno Passenger. The corporal looked at his boots, then at the mud, and laughed for the first time in a week.
Arno Passenger studied the trench map until the candle died, then walked S-S6 in the dark to learn it by heart.
Wendel Melioduff reads Arno Passenger's letters from home out loud, because Arno never learned to read. Wendel leaves out the sad parts. Arno knows.
Arno Passenger was halfway through a story when his listener fell asleep. He counted that as a success.
Day 10. The Hegemony took Blackwater Canal. From the heights Arno Passenger could see the whole Concord line, and for the first time the war looked winnable.
big_shrex: Silas "Button" Shrex walked into R-R16 on Day 9 and asked where the war was. A shell answered before anyone else could.
The report confirmed the Hegemony victory at Blackwater Canal. Silas "Button" Shrex folded the paper so the headline stayed on the outside.
brock_yokley: Clement "Saint" Yokley was a tailor in Esterhaus until the posters went up. He came to R-F11 with a stub of a pencil, and within a day the whole bay knew that he counts everything: steps, shells, stars.
The colonel shook hands with the first hundred, one by one. Clement "Saint" Yokley was number 35. He still remembers how cold the colonel's glove was.
The report confirmed the Concord victory at Verdel Ridge. Clement "Saint" Yokley folded the paper so the headline stayed on the outside.

Clement "Saint" Yokley raised his head for a heartbeat too long at R-F11. The bullet only grazed him. He will not do it again. Shot by Valentin "Crow" Hodnepijumal of the Hegemony (@hodnepijumaloctu).
Clement "Saint" Yokley no longer winces when he lifts his rifle. The medic signed him off with a grunt.

The parcel for Clement "Saint" Yokley contained six left socks. By supper, he had found three men willing to trade. After the loss of Hill 304, Clement "Saint" Yokley helped stack spare sandbags at R-F11. Nobody asked when they would be needed.
Clement "Saint" Yokley has learned to recognize the ration cart by its squeaky wheel. This afternoon, a different squeak caused real disappointment.

Clement "Saint" Yokley held the mirror while Edmund "Whistle" Es shaved. The arrangement survived the shaving but not the comments. The chaplains took Clement "Saint" Yokley in on a busy morning in R-F11. By noon he had learned the first rule of the job, and by evening the second.

A bullet clipped Clement "Saint" Yokley's helmet at R-F11 and took a strip of scalp with it. He bled into his collar, swore, and lay low. Shot by Oskar "Whistle" Jozifanderso of the Hegemony (@jozifanderson). A letter from home found Clement "Saint" Yokley before the night shift. Clement "Saint" Yokley folded it small and kept it close.

Clement "Saint" Yokley took a bullet through the hand and another through the forearm at R-F11, seconds apart. The bearers carried him back with the arm held up like a flag. Shot by Oskar "Whistle" Jozifanderso of the Hegemony (@jozifanderson). A single shot at R-F11. Clement "Saint" Yokley sat down against the trench wall as if to rest, and did not get up. Shot by Oskar "Whistle" Jozifanderso of the Hegemony (@jozifanderson).

Arno "Lucky" Yokley took the same post at R-F11 where Clement "Saint" Yokley stood. He found his brother's initials carved in the wall and put his own beneath them. The First Wave ribbon marked Arno "Lucky" Yokley as an early volunteer. At R-F11, a newcomer asked what those first days had been like.

Arno "Lucky" Yokley fired at a loophole in the enemy wall and heard a shout. It was Edmund "Shadow" Idkdunnoman, grazed. Blackwater Canal is in Hegemony hands. Arno "Lucky" Yokley stopped arguing about the next watch and went to check the stores. The transfer made Arno "Lucky" Yokley a chaplain. He spent the first hour learning where everything belonged, including himself.
christian.__.hensley: Dorian Hensley arrived on Day 9 as a replacement. The men in R-R3 had been fighting for 9 days already and looked at his clean boots like a rumour from another world.
Blackwater Canal has been won. Dorian Hensley listened as the corporal read the news twice, once for the men just off watch.
cody_lahetta: Roland "Button" Lahetta arrived with the evening ration party, carrying a lucky button and a borrowed coat two sizes too big. The new duty roster listed Roland "Button" Lahetta as a machine gunner. He kept checking the old roster until someone took it down.
easy_raider_: Teodor Raider arrived with the Day 9 draft, carrying a pressed cornflower and the news from home, which was old by the time he told it.
Blackwater Canal is in Hegemony hands. Teodor Raider watched the map being corrected and wondered how such a small pencil mark could take so much work.
ebrrrvole: Jakub Ebrrrvole signed the papers with a steady hand. The trench at R-F15 took him in like it takes everyone: without a word.
The colonel shook hands with the first hundred, one by one. Jakub Ebrrrvole was number 65. He still remembers how cold the colonel's glove was.
Konrad Jngaf repaired the strap on Jakub Ebrrrvole's pack. Payment was a biscuit and a promise to stop mentioning the haircut.

Jakub Ebrrrvole received a photograph taken outside the family home. He studied the unfamiliar curtains longer than the faces. The Concord hold Verdel Ridge now, and they can see straight into R-F15. Jakub Ebrrrvole has learned to walk bent double.
Somebody hung a doorbell on the next dugout. Jakub Ebrrrvole went to look. It was a spoon tied to an empty tin.
A bullet clipped Jakub Ebrrrvole's helmet at R-F15 and took a strip of scalp with it. He bled into his collar, swore, and lay low. Shot by Gideon Actioncam of the Concord (@actioncam3000).

Fever took hold of Jakub Ebrrrvole overnight. The medics changed the dressing twice and then called for the bearers. Hill 304 fell to the Hegemony at dusk. Jakub Ebrrrvole helped drag the guns up the slope and slept that night on ground nobody else had held for years.
Jakub Ebrrrvole did not last the night outside the full aid post. The bearers who carried him in carried him out again at dawn.

Another member of the House of Ebrrrvole reached the line: Bastian Ebrrrvole. He asked where Jakub Ebrrrvole had slept, then chose a different corner. Volunteer number 65. The quartermaster pinned the First Wave ribbon on Bastian Ebrrrvole's tunic and said: 'Don't let the mud have it.'

During a lull at the Sunken Road, Bastian Ebrrrvole called across from the Hegemony line. Bastian "Lucky" Vpy answered from the Concord side with a perfect imitation of an officer. Both trenches went quiet.
Bastian Ebrrrvole saw a helmet rise behind the enemy sandbags at R-F15 and fired once. Gideon Actioncam was grazed.
Bastian Ebrrrvole reached up to fix a sandbag at R-F15 and a bullet took the skin off two knuckles. The sandbag got fixed anyway. Shot by Wendel "Smokes" Mrsh of the Concord (@le.mrsh_).

The medic looked at Bastian Ebrrrvole's wound, sniffed it, and sent him back to R-F15. Clean, said the medic. It is the best word a medic knows. Blackwater Canal is in Hegemony hands. Bastian Ebrrrvole watched the map being corrected and wondered how such a small pencil mark could take so much work.
jackmdunn06: Isidor Jackmdunn came up the line in the rain with a photograph gone soft at the edges and nothing else. The sergeant wrote him down as Private and pointed at the mud.
Isidor Jackmdunn was among the first hundred through the depot gates. The First Wave ribbon is the only clean thing he owns.
Isidor Jackmdunn asked to leave the riflemans and serve as a machine gunner. The sergeant looked at him for a long time, then signed the paper without a word.
A flare lit Blackwater Canal like noon. Isidor Jackmdunn counted the seconds until darkness: eleven.

Felix Szymanski of the Hegemony threw a tin of tobacco into the Concord trench with a note: "for the one who sings". Isidor Jackmdunn kept the tin. Word came down the line: Verdel Ridge is ours. Isidor Jackmdunn shook hands with a corporal he had never spoken to. Today, everyone was a friend.
Isidor Jackmdunn fired at a movement across the wire at S-F11. The man went down: Edmund Somosmagios, badly wounded.

A burst of machine-gun fire caught Isidor Jackmdunn in the open at S-F11. The tourniquet held. Whether he holds is another matter. Shot by Norbert Fransinlak of the Hegemony (@fransinlak). Isidor Jackmdunn looked over the parapet at S-F11 for one second too long. The bullet came before the sound. Shot by Norbert Fransinlak of the Hegemony (@fransinlak).

A letter came with Marek Jackmdunn: "I am Isidor Jackmdunn's older brother. I have come to finish what he started." Nobody had the heart to tell him it never finishes. Volunteer number 26. The quartermaster pinned the First Wave ribbon on Marek Jackmdunn's tunic and said: 'Don't let the mud have it.'

Oskar Pbscn cut Marek Jackmdunn's hair with a bayonet and a cracked mirror. It is not good. It is, however, short. Hill 304 is in Hegemony hands. Marek Jackmdunn stopped arguing about the next watch and went to check the stores.
A muddy dog crawled into S-F11 through the wire. Marek Jackmdunn gave it half his bread. It has not left his side since. The men call it Biscuit.
Marek Jackmdunn received the rank of Lance Corporal and a stack of unfinished paperwork. The congratulations lasted less time than the paperwork.
Marek Jackmdunn's hands still remember being a ferryman's hands. Today they mended a broken duckboard as if it were the most important job in the world.
Biscuit has learned to carry messages in a tin on its collar. Marek Jackmdunn is very proud. Biscuit is mainly proud of the biscuits.

Marek Jackmdunn threw a bomb into a Hegemony dugout and dived for cover. When the smoke cleared, Silas Menezes was down and screaming for a medic. (@julio.menezes921) The Hegemony sentry, Silas Zdsh, shouted once. Marek Jackmdunn silenced the shout with the flat of a shovel and was back over the parapet a minute later. (@reza_zdsh) After the loss of Blackwater Canal, Marek Jackmdunn helped stack spare sandbags at S-F11. Nobody asked when they would be needed.
jakub.prokes: After 3 days of war, S-F1 had a place for everything. On Day 4, the men rearranged a shelf to make a place for Albin Prokes.

Albin Prokes (Hegemony) shouted a challenge across to Otto "Saint" Kamdensipple (Concord) at the Sunken Road. The answer was lost under the guns. Nobody repeated the challenge. Mail came up the line with a letter for Albin Prokes. Albin Prokes read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.

Out on the wire with the wiring party. A bullet clipped Albin Prokes's helmet at S-F1 and took a strip of scalp with it. He bled into his collar, swore, and lay low. Mail came up the line with a letter for Albin Prokes. Albin Prokes read it in the dugout and kept the envelope. Hill 304 is in Hegemony hands. Albin Prokes watched the map being corrected and wondered how such a small pencil mark could take so much work.

Albin Prokes no longer winces when he lifts his rifle. The medic signed him off with a grunt. Mail came up the line with a letter for Albin Prokes. Albin Prokes read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.

A report called the trench satisfactory. Albin Prokes invited the author to spend a night in it before signing. Mail came up the line with a letter for Albin Prokes. Albin Prokes read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.

Asked what he wanted after the war, Albin Prokes said a chair. After some thought: a chair nobody else was sitting on. Mail came up the line with a letter for Albin Prokes. Albin Prokes read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.
A bullet went through Albin Prokes's sleeve at S-F1 and took some skin with it. He kept the sleeve. Shot by Quentin Underthrone of the Concord (@underthrone99).

The medic looked at Albin Prokes's wound, sniffed it, and sent him back to S-F1. Clean, said the medic. It is the best word a medic knows. Day 10. The Hegemony took Blackwater Canal. From the heights Albin Prokes could see the whole Concord line, and for the first time the war looked winnable. Mail came up the line with a letter for Albin Prokes. Albin Prokes read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.
justin.earley.73: By the time Matthias Earley reached R-S13, the war was 7 days old and had its own habits. He learned the first one within the hour: keep your head down.

Matthias Earley cut Felix Landon's hair with a bayonet and a cracked mirror. It is not good. It is, however, short. Mail came up the line with a letter for Matthias Earley. Matthias Earley read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.
The parcel for Matthias Earley contained six left socks. By supper, he had found three men willing to trade.
From Blackwater Canal the Hegemony guns have a clear view. Matthias Earley wrote to an old neighbor who promised to keep his garden alive that night and said only: 'We will take it back.'
martin.briton: Bram Briton was a glassblower in Tannenfeld until the posters went up. He came to R-C1 with a bullet that missed him, and within a day the whole squad knew that he keeps feeding the rats.
After the loss of Blackwater Canal, Bram Briton helped stack spare sandbags at R-C1. Nobody asked when they would be needed.
nightrunner289: Walter Nightrunner arrived on Day 9 as a replacement. The men in S-R8 had been fighting for 9 days already and looked at his clean boots like a rumour from another world.
The Hegemony won Blackwater Canal. In S-R8, Walter Nightrunner listened to three explanations and trusted none of them.
oorah961: Quentin Oorah joined the replacements on Day 9. An old hand checked his pack straps before asking his name.
The Hegemony flag went up over Blackwater Canal. Quentin Oorah did not cheer. He sat down on a sandbag and ate his ration slowly, like a man with time again.
somebodynamednile: The quartermaster asked Leopold "Shadow" Somebodyname to sign for the blanket. He examined the blanket and asked whether the holes were included.
The report confirmed that the Hegemony held Blackwater Canal. Leopold "Shadow" Somebodyname read the last line twice, looking for something the first reading had missed.
varyk_leh: "You're late," said the corporal when Leopold "Whistle" Leh arrived on Day 6. "Everyone's late. Get a spade."
Zeno "Ghost" Crackhead held the mirror while Leopold "Whistle" Leh shaved. The arrangement survived the shaving but not the comments.

Leopold "Whistle" Leh sorted the dressings by lamplight. When the next stretcher arrived, he could find everything without looking. A letter from home reached Leopold "Whistle" Leh before dusk. Leopold "Whistle" Leh read it twice and slept a little easier.
Someone asked Leopold "Whistle" Leh to wake them in ten minutes. He had no watch, so he counted slowly and woke them at what felt like ten.
Blackwater Canal is in Hegemony hands. Leopold "Whistle" Leh stopped arguing about the next watch and went to check the stores.
wolfmanantony: Nils Wolfmananton came from Northwick, where there is a river, a church and no mud at all. He talks about all three as if they were people.
A bullet went through Nils Wolfmananton's sleeve at S-F8 and took some skin with it. He kept the sleeve. Shot by Dorian "Whistle" Csllgaks of the Concord (@csllgaks).

The medics cleaned Nils Wolfmananton's wound one last time and pronounced him fit. He is back to full duty at S-F8. The Concord hold Verdel Ridge now, and they can see straight into S-F8. Nils Wolfmananton has learned to walk bent double.

A direct hit on the trench at S-F8. Nils Wolfmananton was the only one they could still help, and only just. Nils Wolfmananton died in the hospital bed despite everything the surgeon tried. a rosary of rough beads was in his hand at the end.
Yann "Smokes" Wolfmananton arrived carrying the family name of Nils Wolfmananton. The corporal asked how to pronounce his first name, and waited for the answer.

The blast lifted Yann "Smokes" Wolfmananton off his feet at S-F8. He came round with a bloody nose and an empty rifle and went back to work. Mail came up the line with a letter for Yann "Smokes" Wolfmananton. Yann "Smokes" Wolfmananton read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.

Yann "Smokes" Wolfmananton sat out the day with a bandaged arm, cleaning every rifle within reach. It was the only job the medic would allow. Mail came up the line with a letter for Yann "Smokes" Wolfmananton. Yann "Smokes" Wolfmananton read it in the dugout and kept the envelope. The Hegemony flag went up over Hill 304. Yann "Smokes" Wolfmananton did not cheer. He sat down on a sandbag and ate his ration slowly, like a man with time again.

A bullet found Yann "Smokes" Wolfmananton at S-F8, high in the shoulder. He went down hard and stayed down. Shot by Zeno "Shadow" Maximus of the Concord (@sleetius_maximus). Yann "Smokes" Wolfmananton died on a stretcher outside the aid post, still waiting for a bed. The medics had nothing left to give him.

A letter came with Dietrich Wolfmananton: "I am Yann "Smokes" Wolfmananton's father. I have come to finish what he started." Nobody had the heart to tell him it never finishes. Orders assigned Dietrich Wolfmananton to work as a machine gunner. The first lesson began with what not to touch.

Dawn watch. Dietrich Wolfmananton put a round across no man's land and the enemy line went quiet: Zeno "Shadow" Maximus, badly wounded. A bullet clipped Dietrich Wolfmananton's helmet at S-F8 and took a strip of scalp with it. He bled into his collar, swore, and lay low. Shot by Otto Valiantlyval of the Concord (@valiantlyvaliancy). Mail came up the line with a letter for Dietrich Wolfmananton. Dietrich Wolfmananton read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.

Dietrich Wolfmananton was carrying water up to S-F8 when a bullet hit him in the leg. The water reached the trench. Dietrich Wolfmananton did not. Shot by Otto Valiantlyval of the Concord (@valiantlyvaliancy). Mail came up the line with a letter for Dietrich Wolfmananton. Dietrich Wolfmananton read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.

Dietrich Wolfmananton spent the day on a stretcher outside the aid post, waiting for a bed to come free. The bearers brought water twice. Mail came up the line with a letter for Dietrich Wolfmananton. Dietrich Wolfmananton read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.

No bed, no surgeon, just a medic with a kit and a lot of patience. Dietrich Wolfmananton recovered anyway and is back at S-F8. Victory at Blackwater Canal. Dietrich Wolfmananton let himself talk about leave for the first time in days. Mail came up the line with a letter for Dietrich Wolfmananton. Dietrich Wolfmananton read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.
